1	# ADR-0006: Near-duplicate articles alias, never merge
2	
3	## Status
4	
5	Accepted (2026-07-10, not yet implemented).
6	
7	## Decision
8	
9	When two URLs carry nearly the same text (syndication, aggregator republish, small edits), both articles keep their own ref and text; a near-duplicate detector links the copy to a canonical via a `duplicate_of` pointer. Canonical selection: higher Provider tier, then longer body, then earliest acquisition. Only canonical articles are chunked and indexed; duplicates stay dereferenceable. Aliasing wins because a wrong link is deleted in one statement, while a wrong merge corrupts identity irreversibly. The case is already live in the corpus: the same WIRETWO story was acquired twice on 2026-05-06 under two section URLs, with a one-hyphen title edit and a changed body; URL, title, and content dedup all missed it (title dedup was structurally inert because neither acquisition carried a published date).
10	
11	## Considered options
12	
13	- Hard merge at ingest: rejected, false merges are unrecoverable and thresholds would need tuning against live aggregator data first.
14	- Retrieval-time dedup only: rejected, the corpus double-counts syndicated stories and every listing consumer sees duplicates.
15	
16	## Consequences
17	
18	- Provider tier is a small static checked-in config: a ranking feature and canonical-selection input, never a verification verdict.
19	- A canonical flip is a ref-visible event: the demoted copy's chunks retire as superseded and the promoted copy gets chunked.
